long_synopsis: This week brought no single dramatic rupture, only accumulation: a president suing a newspaper, a Speaker sending Congress home early, and agencies erasing their own expert capacity. New Epstein-related reporting triggered lawsuits against the Wall Street Journal, selective grand jury disclosure requests, and a shuttered House floor. Immigration enforcement expanded sharply, with a $1.26 billion detention contract, National Guard support, and nearly three thousand Los Angeles arrests. Accusations that Obama committed treason moved rhetoric into a DOJ strike force. Universities faced funding coercion, crypto policy blurred into personal enrichment, and archives were selectively sealed or released. Courts remained the most consistent obstacle, blocking birthright-citizenship changes and protecting due process. The Democracy Clock moved only 0.1 minutes, from 7:41 p.m. to 7:41 p.m., reflecting density spread across many fronts rather than one dominant event.
